paragraphs: Robin Radar Systems makes 360 degree, 3D radar systems that detect, track and classify small flying objects such as birds, bats and drones. It sells them to aviation, defence, security and ecology teams that want a full view of their airspace. Its two main products are IRIS, a 3D drone radar in a 29 kg package, and MAX, a 3D bird detection radar.

IRIS uses micro-doppler classification and deep neural network technology to distinguish blades and rotating parts. It combines 360 degree views, 60 degree elevation and a 5 km instrumented range. A software-only update, Long-Range Mode, lets operators switch between 5 km and 12 km instrumented ranges in minutes. MAX pairs with two software interfaces, Bird Viewer for live airspace and Report Viewer for historical analysis. Airports, airfields and wind farms use the bird and bat radars to react to hazards as they emerge.

The name comes from a 1980 project by the Dutch research institute TNO to prevent bird strikes on Royal Netherlands Air Force planes. Siete Hamminga, now CEO, spun the technology out of TNO in 2010 to found the company. It reports more than 300 radars deployed worldwide and a staff of 150 or more people. In 2024 its shareholders reached an acquisition agreement with the Dutch investment company Parcom. Scarecrow, a maker of bird dispersal and data logging systems based on bio-acoustic technology, is a Robin company.

quote.text: Deployed in mission-critical defence and security operations across the globe, IRIS is purpose-built to meet the needs of tactical operators in the field.
